# American-Held Prisoners-of-War in Balayan, 1900-01

Batangas History

15 Sep, 2024

Below is a transcribed list of mostly Batangueño prisoners-of-war held by the United States Army at a facility in the municipality of Balayan in late 1900 up to the middle of 1901. At this time, the Philippine-American War was still raging and would not end, at least officially, until April 1902 with the surrender of General Miguel Malvar.

Majority of the prisoners in the record were “insurgents” — the term signifying that, as far as the Americans were concerned, they had set up a legitimate colonial government and that the Filipino revolutionaries were “rebels” against it. Of course, from the Filipino point of view, the Americans had no right to be in the Philippines in the first place.

There were others who were imprisoned for what may sound like innocuous offenses such as “possession of a bolo,” which although a deadly weapon was also used in the farm; or possession of “suspicious papers.”

Towards the end of the document, prisoners were described to have been arrested for what were apparently civilian offenses such as the theft of a pony, wife-beating, or stealing from stores. ^{35} Or "Diokno."

Después de la batalla, el grupo de 15 guerrilleros que encabezaba tuvo un segundo enfrentamiento con fuerzas federales al mando del coronel Ibáñez. Semanas después fue apresado en San Antonio, Tex.
